He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona Wildcats]]. He was named first-team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-12]] and was voted the [[Pac-12 Conference Men's Basketball Defensive Player of the Year|Pac-12 Defensive Player of the Year]] after his junior season. ==Early life== Koloko is a native of [[Babouantou]] in the west region of Cameroon who grew up in Douala, Cameroon and attended Collège Libermann in his hometown.{{cite web|first=Yvan|last=Ngon|title=Christian Koloko, révélation Camerounaise enviée en NBA|url=https://cameroonvoice.com/sport/2020/03/07/christian-koloko-revelation-camerounaise-enviee-en-nba/|website=CameroonVoice.com|date=7 March 2020|access-date=23 November 2021|language=fr}} He grew up playing [[association football|football]] and started playing basketball at age 12.{{cite web|first=C. J.|last=Holmes|title=Christian Koloko is 'still a baby in this game,' but Arizona is pleased with the freshman's steady progress|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/1455900/2019/12/13/christian-koloko-is-still-a-baby-in-this-game-but-arizona-is-pleased-with-the-freshmans-steady-progress/|work=[[The Athletic]]|date=13 December 2019|access-date=23 November 2021}} In 2017, Koloko moved to the United States to play basketball for [[Birmingham High School]] in [[Lake Balboa, Los Angeles|Lake Balboa, California]] as a junior, despite not speaking English at first.{{cite web|first=Bruce|last=Pascoe|title=Seen and heard: Christian Koloko, still adapting to life in US, has Arizona on his radar|url=https://tucson.com/sports/arizonawildcats/basketball/seen-and-heard-christian-koloko-still-adapting-to-life-in-us-has-arizona-on-his/collection_60ca9daa-921f-11e8-b169-3ffb2fb49abc.html#3|work=[[Arizona Daily Star]]|date=27 July 2018|access-date=23 November 2021}} For his senior season, he transferred to [[Sierra Canyon School]] in [[Chatsworth, Los Angeles|Chatsworth, California]], where he was teammates with [[Cassius Stanley]], [[Kenyon Martin Jr.]] and [[Scotty Pippen Jr.|Scotty Pippen Jr]].{{cite web|first=Ryan|last=Kelapire|title=Arizona block machine Christian Koloko wants to show he's more than a project|url=https://www.azdesertswarm.com/basketball/2020/1/8/21056227/christian-koloko-arizona-wildcats-basketball-block-depth-chart-project-freshman|work=Arizona Desert Swarm|date=8 January 2020|access-date=23 November 2021}} Koloko helped his team claim its second straight Open Division state title. A four-star recruit, he committed to playing college basketball for [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]] over offers from [[California Golden Bears men's basketball|California]], [[Northwestern Wildcats men's basketball|Northwestern]], [[Vanderbilt Commodores men's basketball|Vanderbilt]], [[Harvard Crimson men's basketball|Harvard]] and [[Princeton Tigers men's basketball|Princeton]].{{cite web|first=Bruce|last=Pascoe|title=From Cameroon to Cats: Arizona gets commitment from 6-foot-10 Christian Koloko|url=https://tucson.com/sports/arizonawildcats/basketball/from-cameroon-to-cats-arizona-gets-commitment-from-6-foot-10-christian-koloko/article_19ecd5a3-22b0-5601-b79d-da7661a407ce.html|website=Tucson.com|date=23 September 2018|access-date=23 November 2021}} ==College career== As a freshman at Arizona, Koloko averaged 2.3 points and 2.4 rebounds per game.{{cite web|first=Matt|last=Moreno|title=Offseason limitations could slow development for Arizona's Christian Koloko|url=https://arizona.rivals.com/news/offseason-limitations-could-slow-development-for-arizona-s-christian-koloko|website=Rivals.com|date=11 May 2020|access-date=23 November 2021}} In his sophomore season, he averaged 5.3 points and 4.8 rebounds per game.{{cite web|first=Troy|last=Hutchison|title=Arizona center Christian Koloko named Pac-12 Player of the Week|url=https://arizona.rivals.com/news/arizona-center-christian-koloko-named-pac-12-player-of-the-week|website=Rivals.com|date=23 November 2021|access-date=23 November 2021}} On 21 November 2021, Koloko posted a career-high 22 points, seven rebounds and four blocks in an 80–62 win over fourth-ranked [[2021–22 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|Michigan]] at the [[Roman Main Event]] title game, earning tournament MVP honors.{{cite web|first=Brian J.|last=Pedersen|title=Christian Koloko outplays Michigan's Hunter Dickinson as Arizona cruises past Wolverines|url=https://www.azdesertswarm.com/2021/11/21/22795837/arizona-wildcats-christian-koloko-mens-basketball-michigan-wolverines-2021-hunter-dickinson-vegas|work=Arizona Desert Swarm|date=21 November 2021|access-date=23 November 2021}} As a junior, he was named [[Pac-12 Conference Men's Basketball Defensive Player of the Year|Pac-12 Defensive Player of the Year]], [[Pac-12]] Most Improved Player, and first-team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-12]].{{cite press release|title=2021-22 Pac-12 Men's Basketball All-Conference honors and Annual Performance Awards, presented by Nextiva|url=https://pac-12.com/news/2022/3/8/2021-22-pac-12-mens-basketball-all-conference-honors-and-annual-performance.aspx|website=Pac-12.com|publisher=[[Pac-12 Conference]]|date=March 8, 2022|access-date=March 8, 2022}} On 18 April 2022, Koloko declared for the [[2022 NBA draft]], forgoing his remaining college eligibility.{{cite web|title=Arizona junior Christian Koloko declares for 2022 NBA draft|url=https://therookiewire.usatoday.com/2022/04/18/arizona-christian-koloko-2022-nba-draft/|work=The Rookie Wire|date=18 April 2022|access-date=19 June 2022}}{{cite web|title=Arizona C Christian Koloko declares for 2022 NBA Draft|url=https://arizonasports.com/story/3090027/arizona-christian-koloko-declares-for-2022-nba-draft/|work=Arizona Sports|date=18 April 2022|access-date=19 June 2022}} ==Professional career== ===Toronto Raptors (2022–2024)=== Koloko was selected with the 33rd overall pick in the [[2022 NBA draft]] by the [[Toronto Raptors]].{{cite web|title=Raptors pick Christian Koloko with 33rd pick|url=https://www.tsn.ca/toronto-raptors-christian-koloko-nba-draft-no-33-pick-1.1817025|website=TSN.ca|agency=The Canadian Press|date=23 June 2022|access-date=24 June 2022}} On 26 August 2022, Koloko signed a rookie-scale contract with the Raptors.{{cite web|first=M.|last=Beloso|title=RAPTORS SIGN SECOND ROUND PICK KOLOKO|url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/news/raptors-sign-second-round-pick-koloko|website=NBA.com|date=26 August 2022|access-date=25 September 2022}} As a rookie, he appeared in 58 games, averaging 3.1 points, 2.9 rebounds, one block and 13.8 minutes per contest. In April 2023, he developed a [[blood clot]] health issue that kept him on the sideline for half of the season. On 17 January 2024, Koloko was waived by the Raptors, as he wasn't cleared to play and the team was looking to make space on the roster after the [[Pascal Siakam]] trade.{{cite web|title=RAPTORS COMPLETE TRADE WITH INDIANA|url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/news/raptors-complete-trade-with-indiana-2|website=NBA.com|date=17 January 2024|access-date=18 January 2024}} A day later, he was put into NBA's fitness-to-play panel due to the seriousness of the blood clot issue, meaning no teams can claim waiver to sign him until he is medically cleared to play.{{Cite web |date=19 January 2024 |title=Raptors prez: Koloko's status 'in hands of NBA' |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/39339008 |access-date=19 January 2024 |website=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press}} ===Los Angeles Lakers (2024–2025)=== On 16 September 2024, Koloko signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]], although he still needed to be medically cleared by the NBA and sign a risk waiver to return to the league.{{cite web|title=Lakers Sign Christian Koloko to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/news/lakers-sign-christian-koloko-to-two-way-contract-091624|website=NBA.com|date=16 September 2024|access-date=16 September 2024}} On 29 October 2024, he received clearance from the NBA's fitness-to-play panel to start practicing and return to play.{{Cite web |date=29 October 2024 |title=Lakers' Christian Koloko medically cleared to play, sources say |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/42074108/lakers-christian-koloko-medically-cleared-play-sources-say |access-date=29 October 2024 |website=ESPN.com}} On 6 November 2024, he made his Lakers debut against the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] with [[Anthony Davis]] unavailable to play and [[Christian Wood]] still recovering from arthroscopic surgery on his left knee. On 13 November 2024, [[Jaxson Hayes]] was diagnosed with a left ankle sprain, which increased Koloko's playing time. On 26 November 2025, Koloko was waived by the Lakers, following the signing of [[Drew Timme]].{{cite web | title=Los Angeles Lakers Sign Forward Drew Timme to Two-Way Contract | website=NBA | date=2025-11-25 | url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/news/lakers-sign-forward-drew-timme-to-two-way-contract | access-date=2025-12-06}} === Austin Spurs (2025) === On 15 December 2025, Koloko was acquired from the player pool by the [[Austin Spurs]] of the [[NBA G League]].{{Cite web |title=AUSTIN SPURS ACQUIRE CHRISTIAN KOLOKO |url=https://austin.gleague.nba.com/news/austin-spurs-acquire-christian-koloko |access-date=2025-12-25 |website=Austin Spurs |language=en}} === Memphis Grizzles (2025–2026) === On 22 December 2025, Koloko signed a 10-day contract (hardship exception) with the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] due to injuries on the roster,{{Cite web |title=Memphis Grizzlies Injury Report |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/team/injuries/_/name/mem/memphis-grizzlies}} adding depth at center. On 2 January 2026, Koloko signed a second 10-day contract with the Grizzlies.{{Cite web |title=Grizzlies Sign Christian Koloko to Second 10-Day Contract {{!}} Memphis Grizzlies |url=https://grizzlies.com/news/grizzlies-sign-christian-koloko-to-second-10-day-contract |access-date=2026-01-02 |website=grizzlies.com |language=en}} === Atlanta Hawks (2026) === On 16 January 2026, Koloko signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Atlanta Hawks]], splitting time with their [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[College Park Skyhawks]].{{Cite web |title=Atlanta Hawks Sign Center Christian Koloko to Two-Way Contract {{!}} Atlanta Hawks |url=https://hawks.com/news/atlanta-hawks-sign-center-christian-koloko-to-two-way-contract |access-date=2026-01-16 |website=hawks.com |language=en}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} ===NBA=== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| {{nbay|2022}} | style="text-align:left;"| [[2022–23 Toronto Raptors season|Toronto]] | '''58''' || '''19''' || 13.8 || .480 || '''.083''' || .627 || 2.9 || .5 || .4 || 1.0 || '''3.1''' |- | style="text-align:left;"| {{nbay|2024}} | style="text-align:left;"| [[2024–25 Los Angeles Lakers season|L.A.
